World imports/exports are explicit component boundaries; no import means the component cannot invoke that host API. This applies to WASM-hosted components, not arbitrary host-native executables.
Imports can be checked against compatible exports before composition.

A useful primary language reference: child tasks stay within scope; groups wait for all children; cancellation propagates but is cooperative. This is a semantic precedent, not a Rust implementation API.
Transport binds JSON-RPC framing, metadata, cancellation and termination. Current spec offers newline-delimited stdio and Streamable HTTP; transport does not define applet behavior.
One newline-delimited JSON-RPC message per line; stdout must contain protocol messages only; stderr is logging.

Per-request POST with JSON or request-scoped SSE; cancellation by disconnect; current revision has no protocol session or resumable SSE; recommends Origin validation, localhost binding and authentication.

The 2026-07-28 revision is stateless: each request carries its protocol version and the old initialize/session handshake is retired; earlier revisions retain a different compatibility era. Pin and test the intended revisions.
QML has typed property definitions, reactive bindings, typed signals and property-change signals. That does not supply a process/runtime adapter or lifecycle contract.
Bubblewrap is a sandbox construction tool, not a complete policy; security depends on caller-supplied arguments.
The macOS sandbox-exec command is explicitly deprecated; avoid presenting it as a supported portable certification path.
Google Pub/Sub limits exactly-once delivery to pull subscriptions and a region; publish-side duplicates and operational caveats remain.
Safe retry depends on participant API idempotency semantics and request tokens; a coordinator alone cannot make arbitrary side effects exactly once.

items.title: No end-to-end transactional mutations
items.audit_claim: Multi-command changes to configuration files, registries, and external systems can partially succeed.
items.evidence_note: POSIX.1-2024 specifies atomic namespace visibility for rename/directory operations, while separately warning that directory updates may not be durable after crash. The candidate `fs.transaction` journal coordinates a bounded set of file edits with per-file CAS and compensation/recovery; changes become visible sequentially, not as one all-files atomic commit, and external registries/services are not participants. Candidate owner/worktree evidence: Owner reports path/text/arithmetic/filesystem/JSON/JSONC core applets, typed manifest ports, and bounded journaled transaction/unlink work. Isolated applet tests pass 14/14 in a scratch crate; `cargo clippy --offline ... -- -D warnings` passes. A separate extracted transaction harness using the same transaction source plus a platform shim passes 6/6; it is not the main crate. All 31 core manifests parse. Transaction metadata is intentionally capped at 1 MiB, while before/after blobs have a separate 16 MiB aggregate cap. These are source-level harness results, not an integrated end-to-end result. The JSONC helper makes no VS Code `jsonc-parser` compatibility claim: it is bounded to 16 MiB/depth 256, whole-document strict parse, comments/trailing commas, active top-level object keys; `set` updates the last duplicate and `remove` removes all duplicates while preserving unaffected source slices. It lacks VS Code fault-tolerant recovery/diagnostics and nested/array path-edit semantics. Filesystem advisory locks only coordinate cooperating writers, parent dirs are trusted, rename has a non-cooperating-writer race, Unix preserves mode bits only, and no multi-file atomicity is claimed.
items.closure_evidence_required: Specify the narrow safety/recovery contract and fault model; inject failure/race/tampering at each boundary and retain platform-specific evidence. A single-file atomic operation does not prove a cross-applet transaction.

items.title: No exactly-once external effects
items.audit_claim: A crashed process may have succeeded externally before its completion was recorded.
items.owner: recovery_workflows (bounded compensation only; universal guarantee impossible)
items.evidence_note: A crash between an external side effect and durable completion leaves an unknown outcome. Candidate file transactions can reconcile recorded before/after file hashes and offer compensation, but apply files sequentially and cannot yield universal multi-file atomicity or power-loss durability (Windows directory sync is a no-op in this candidate). RFC 9110 §9.2.2 says clients should not automatically retry non-idempotent requests without a way to know the request was unapplied or actually idempotent. The remote applet client therefore sends POST once; explicit idempotency keys only work if the server honors a declared scope. Arbitrary outside effects remain impossible to guarantee exactly once. Candidate owner/worktree evidence: Implementation lane has been assigned; exact code paths and focused validation have not yet been reported at ledger refresh.
items.closure_evidence_required: Replace the universal claim with a scoped contract (e.g. idempotency key, transactional participant, durable outbox, or compensation); inject a crash across the uncertainty window and document participant limits.

research_sources.finding: Google Pub/Sub limits exactly-once delivery to pull subscriptions and a region; publish-side duplicates and operational caveats remain.
Safe retry depends on participant API idempotency semantics and request tokens; a coordinator alone cannot make arbitrary side effects exactly once.

Idempotent request methods can be retried after ambiguous connection failure; a client should not automatically retry a non-idempotent request unless it can establish request semantics are idempotent or that the original request was never applied.

research_sources.finding: The base protocol uses ASCII CRLF headers, requires Content-Length measured in body bytes, and defaults the JSON-RPC body to UTF-8. This wire claim does not establish full LSP feature coverage.

research_sources.source_version: LSP 3.17 specification
research_sources.finding: Position line/character are zero based; character units use negotiated PositionEncodingKind. UTF-16 must be supported and is the default when no encoding is negotiated; position-encoding negotiation was added in 3.17.

items.title: No agent-directed contract matching

Bounds include 64 KiB headers, 8 MiB messages, 4 MiB/doc, 32 MiB aggregate open text, 256 docs, 128 edits/change and 10k rename edits; duplicate Content-Length and stale versions are rejected, changes staged atomically. items.title: No applet compatibility diagnostics
items.audit_claim: An AI can't yet get an actionable compiler message explaining a mismatch between two output/input port schemas.
items.evidence_note: Contract schemas can help detect type mismatches. Actionable producer-to-consumer diagnostics need an actual graph/type-check implementation and negative tests. Candidate owner/worktree evidence: Owner reports schema types bytes/text/path/integer/boolean/json/record, recursive records, strict duplicate-key JSON, raw/json framing, opt-in trim-one-LF, and path nonempty/NUL checks. A02/E01 partially covered; multi-output/event graph, version-range negotiation, backend-neutral identity, and native pipe/backpressure semantics remain open; no green integrated test result reported. Owner reports `cargo test --test graph_contracts --test graph_runtime` passes 17/17 (8 contracts + 9 runtime). Coverage includes typed mismatch and cycle rejection, manifest/renderer port schemas, bounded queue policies, lossless multicast/merge and explicit lossy policies, timer cancel/generation/revision, stale-event filtering, panic-close, message/collection bounds, shared `invoke_applet`, and taint propagation. This supports partial closure only: no implicit conversions; native stream remains `Records<Bytes>`; `listen to stdin` is unsupported and applet `listen to` still uses the finite stream runner; typed JSONL decoding and generic applet event outputs are absent. Graph node I/O is a bounded resident worker (default max 64); tests do not establish arbitrary backend lifecycle or stress/leak performance. `GraphPlan::to_json`/`to_dot` expose topology, not a visual UI. Delivery/drop semantics are explicit; lossy policies intentionally drop events, so no guaranteed-delivery claim.
